newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US agree need for Japan demand-led growth.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US agree need for Japan demand-led growth.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin agreed in a meeting on Friday that Japan should promote economic growth led by domestic demand, a MOF official told reporters.
Asked if the rise in Japan's February trade surplus was a temporary fluctuation, the MOF official said:
"Yes that's right." He added that macro-economics was not a science that could be exactly fine-tuned.

Mitsuzuka and Rubin agreed that they would like to avoid a drastic increase in Japan's current account surplus, although the figure may fluctuate from time to time, the Ministry of Finance official said.
"The two sides are in agreement that we want to avoid a drastic increase as an overall trend," the official said.
The official also said that the two agreed it was important for Japan to promote economic growth led by domestic demand.
Rubin was greatly interested in Japan's deregulatory measures, especially those concerning Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms, the official said.
"Secretary Rubin welcomed Japan's vigorous efforts in carrying out deregulation, such as the reforms in six major areas (announced at the end of March)," the official said.
Rubin also welcomed Japan's efforts to strengthen its financial system, such as the measures hammered out to increase the liquidity of collateralised land, the official said.
Mitsuzuka and Rubin agreed that it was important for the two countries to maintain a strong cooperative relationship on economic and financial matters, the official said.

Although Mitsuzuka and Rubin did not specifically discuss currencies, the MOF official who briefed reporters said that maintaining strong cooperative ties on financial matters would certainly include matters related to foreign exchange.
Mitsuzuka also explained to Rubin that Japan's economy was on a solid footing and that Japan was vigorously tackling its bad loan problem, the official said.
